Test a robust weighted scheme using softmax over negative error to emphasize better models while dampening the influence of noisy ones, given the unstable ranking and noisy regime.
The series has unstable rankings and many outliers; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of extreme models and improve robustness.
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated groups, so a robust median may outperform trimmed mean by reducing influence of outliers and correlated errors.
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a robust dba over the full pool might outperform the median.
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated errors; testing a weighted combination on the trimmed 7‑model pool should exploit the best performers while reducing noise.
Try a softmax‐based weighted combo over the high‑performing subset (pool4) to see if a more aggressive weighting improves on the median leader.
average the 7 most stable, diverse models
Ranking is unstable and several models have correlated errors; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting could exploit the fact that different models win at different horizons.
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a trimmed mean over a smaller, more diverse subset (pool4) may reduce noise while keeping robustness.
The series shows unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a simple robust median over a reduced, correlated‑group‑aware pool may outperform the full‑pool median.

decision.justification: Selected 'median' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.6969. Series context: trend strength 0.0881 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.115); 12 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 21.444.
